key_insight: PV can look highly energy-positive at the panel level, but its system-level EROI drops sharply once grid reliability and firming are included.
engineering_relevance: For power-system design, the decisive constraint is not only how much renewable electricity is generated, but whether it can be delivered continuously with enough net energy left after storage, backup, and fuel-supply overheads.
method: Fleet-equivalent benchmark accounting model, not a simulation or optimization.
Compares unfirmed renewables against battery, hydrogen, and gas-firmed supply chains.
Uses illustrative Central European wind-PV mix with lifecycle energy and GWP accounting.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports EROI falling from 10.7–16.0 unfirmed to 0.7–2.3 with 24 h battery balancing, 3.4–7.7 for seasonal hydrogen, and emissions rising to 80–289 gCO2eq/kWh for hydrogen/battery-hydrogen firming.
watch_item: The benchmark uses favorable orientation, siting, curtailment, and delivery assumptions, so real deployments are likely to perform worse than the reported upper-bound values.
paper_title: Photovoltaics beyond the panel: system-level net energy under grid and firming constraints
